frontier.hypothesis: The pure-C axis is closed and the gap is a SOURCE-MODEL gap whose statement is now one notch sharper than the ledger's: the original source held two INDEPENDENTLY MATERIALISED, simultaneously live address values for D_80106A73 -- not merely two address objects.
frontier.mechanism: One C object gives one live value at a time (tools/gcc-2.7.2/global.c:426, one allocno per pseudo, no live-range splitting in 2.7.2). Two objects obtained by a COPY give a second pseudo that is a dependent value: measured this session at sandbox 8 / 51 insns, carrying a `move` plus a fresh `lui` the target does not have, with block 1's register naming still inverted. Only three objects, each initialised from the symbol, ever reached 0. So the escalation packet's claim should be the stronger and more specific one -- the target's second base is materialised from the symbol before block 1's store -- and the fallback 'maybe two objects of any kind would do it' is now measured dead.
frontier.next_probe: Escalation-modality session ONLY. Do NOT re-run the pure-C ladder and do NOT re-run the permuter: s19/s20 saturated the structural and address-pseudo dimensions by hand, and s21 has now saturated the random-structural neighbourhood from BOTH sides of the ceiling (44,626 iterations at the floor with one object, 37,153 from e1 reaching only 8 with two). Lead the packet with the independent-materialisation statement plus this session's pricing (a copied second object is worth 3 points and stops at 8), then evaluate the two endgame-lock gates -- gate 1 already FAILS (scan_hand_coded tier=LOW, 0/8); gate 2 needs a CITED SOTN-master precedent where multiple C handles on one global are load-bearing -- and if both fail, file the standing-ruling REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE entry at the single-handle floor of 10.
